long_job_verdict.reason: FJsEnvImpl::UvRunOnce runs uv_run on the game thread. While a long native call holds that thread the pipe is never read, so a job_status query is not merely refused by the active-command guard, it is never received until the work it asks about has finished. No client-side or TypeScript change can work around a blocked game thread.

hook_hypothesis.evidence: core.hooksPath is empty; .git/hooks contains only .sample files; .githooks is empty; .claude/settings.json configures exactly three hooks (SessionStart banner, guard-legacy-http and guard-destructive, both PreToolUse) and none of them run git.
hook_hypothesis.note: Recorded because it was my stated blocker and it was wrong. Guessing at a cause and then halting on the guess is worse than not guessing.

remaining_hypothesis.statement: Concurrent subagents sharing one .git. Git worktrees share a single object store and HEAD-per-worktree; a lane whose shell cwd resolved to the main tree rather than its own worktree would commit to the integration branch under the repository identity, which matches every symptom.
remaining_hypothesis.status: UNPROVEN. Consistent with all four witnesses but not demonstrated.
remaining_hypothesis.practical_mitigation: Run lanes SEQUENTIALLY, one live agent at a time, until it is demonstrated. Wave one ran three concurrent lanes and produced no such report; wave two ran three concurrent lanes and produced four. That correlation is suggestive, not proof.

INCIDENT.blocker_status: DOWNGRADED. Content is verified intact and npm run verify passes at 208 tools. The risk is misattribution, not corruption, and sequential lanes mitigate it.

remaining_actionable.product_defect_found: rename_component is NOT convergent. After a batch renames Lamp to Beacon, rerunning the same batch fails with "operation 5 (rename_component Lamp -> Beacon): 'Beacon' is already taken by a different component." A rename whose source is gone and whose target already exists is ALREADY SATISFIED, and the satisfied-check must say so instead of reading the existing target as a collision. Same class of bug lane A hit on links: the predicate answers the pre-state question rather than the post-state one. This breaks convergence, which the tool is annotated destructiveIdempotent for.
